name: 2 Peter

facts.author: The apostle Simon Peter, as the letter itself says (1:1). He writes as one who saw the glory of Jesus on the holy mountain (1:16-18).
facts.audience: The same believers to whom Peter had written his first letter (3:1), and all who share the same precious faith

about: Peter wrote this second letter near the end of his life. He knew that he would soon lay aside his body, as the Lord Jesus had shown him (1:14), and he wanted to remind the believers of the truth so that they would remember it after he was gone.

By His divine power God has given us all that we need to live and to live godly lives (1:3). So believers should add to their faith goodness, knowledge, self-control, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and love. The gospel is no clever story: Peter himself heard the Father's voice honouring the Son, and the prophets spoke from God as the Holy Spirit moved them (1:21).

Yet false teachers would come, greedy and proud, leading many astray. God judged the angels who sinned, the world of Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah, and He knows how to rescue the godly. Some mock and ask why the Lord has not come. Peter answers that the Lord is patient, not wanting anyone to perish (3:9). The day of the Lord will come like a thief, and God's people look for new heavens and a new earth.

themes.title: Growing in grace
themes.text: Faith should grow and bear fruit; believers are to grow in the grace and knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ (3:18).

themes.title: The true word of God
themes.text: The gospel rests on eyewitnesses and on Scripture, which came from God and not from the will of man.

themes.title: Beware of false teachers
themes.text: Those who twist the truth and live for pleasure will face God's judgement, just as in the days of Noah and Lot.

themes.title: The Lord will come
themes.text: The delay of His coming is God's patience, giving time to repent, so believers should live holy and peaceful lives while they wait.

outline.title: Greeting; growing in faith and godliness
